transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I came in because, well, my mind just keeps going blank at the worst possible times. Like, I'll be at work—I'm a flagger—and I will look at the road-closure forms, or even just hold my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps. It's like I completely forget how to do things I have done for years.
When these moments happen, do you experience any physical sensations, like jerking movements, lip smacking, or a feeling of losing consciousness?

No, I don't think so. I don't have any jerking movements or anything like that. And I don't feel like I'm passing out or losing consciousness. I'm still there, awake, my brain just... stops working. It's just a complete blank.
During these moments when your mind goes blank, do you feel as though you are observing yourself from outside your body or that the world around you feels unreal or dreamlike?

No, I don't feel like that at all. I'm definitely still in my body. And everything around me looks normal and real—I know I'm standing on the road, I can see the cars and everything. It's not like a dream. It's just... the thoughts are completely gone. I'm right there, but my head is just empty.
Do you find that these episodes of your mind going blank happen more frequently when you are feeling particularly stressed or anxious?

I haven't really noticed a connection like that. I mean, sure, being on the road can be stressful sometimes, but these blank moments just seem to happen whenever. It doesn't feel like being stressed out brings them on. They just happen out of nowhere.
After these blank moments pass, do you feel confused or tired for a few minutes before you are able to get back to your normal tasks?

No, not really. I mean... once it passes, it just passes. I don't feel tired or mixed up afterwards. My thoughts just sort of start up again, and I go right back to whatever I was doing—like holding my sign or watching the crosswalk. It's really just that gap in the middle where nothing is there, but right after that, I'm fine to keep working.
About how many seconds or minutes would you say these blank episodes usually last?

They don't last very long. Maybe just a few seconds, or a minute at most. But it's enough to mess me up. That's actually why I came in... my mind keeps going blank at the worst possible times. Like, I'll be looking at the road-closure forms, or holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps I've done for years. It's like my thinking just stops.
When these episodes occur, have any of your coworkers ever mentioned that you looked like you were staring off into space or that you didn't respond when they tried to talk to you?

No, nobody has ever said anything like that to me. I don't think I'm staring off or ignoring people. It's just that inside my head, the thoughts stop. As far as I know, my coworkers haven't noticed anything weird.
During these blank moments, have you ever noticed any unusual sensations, such as a strange taste in your mouth, a rising feeling in your stomach, or a sudden, intense smell?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No strange tastes or smells, and my stomach feels fine. It's really just the thoughts stopping, nothing else physical that I can think of.
Are there any specific thoughts, worries, or memories that tend to cross your mind just before your mind goes blank?

Not really, no. I've tried to figure out if there's a pattern, but... it doesn't seem tied to any specific worry or memory. I could just be standing there, completely focused on the traffic, feeling fine, and then... it just happens. The thoughts just shut off. There's no warning or specific thing I'm thinking about right before it hits.

Do you feel that your ability to move or control your limbs is affected in any way while your mind is blank, or are you still able to physically continue your work tasks even though your mind feels empty?

No, my body works just fine. I can still hold up the stop sign or wave the cars through. I don't freeze up or lose control of my arms or anything like that. I just keep doing the motions of the job, even when my head is completely empty. It's just the thoughts that stop, not my body.
When your mind goes blank, does it feel like your brain is just too tired or sluggish to process information, or does it feel like the thoughts are simply being erased?

It feels more like... well, it's why I came in to see you, honestly. It's not just feeling tired. My mind just keeps going blank at the worst times. Like, I'll be looking at the road-closure forms I have to fill out, or even just holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps I've done for years. It's like the thoughts are just gone.
During these moments when your mind goes blank, do you feel like you are mentally 'checked out' or distant from the people and things around you?

I wouldn't say I feel checked out or distant, exactly. I'm still there, I still see the cars and the people. It's not like I'm floating away or disconnected from what's happening around me. It's just... the thinking part stops. I'm still present, just empty-headed for a minute.
After the episode is over, do you have any gaps in your memory for what you were doing or what was happening around you while your mind was blank?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't lose time or black out or anything. When it's over, I know I was just standing there... I remember seeing the cars go by and I know what was happening around me. It's just that I wasn't thinking anything while it happened. So, no, there aren't any missing pieces in my memory.
When your mind goes blank, do you feel like you are actively trying to think but just can't, or does it feel like your brain has simply stopped trying to think altogether?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I don't think I'm actively trying to think... it's more like I just realize nothing is happening up there. I don't know if my brain stopped trying or if I just can't. It's just blank.

Does this 'blank' sensation happen more often when you are actively trying to read or process the information on your road-closure forms than when you are just performing the routine task of holding your sign?

It definitely happens more when I'm trying to look at the paperwork. Actually, that's the main reason I came in to see you. My mind just keeps going blank at the worst possible times. I'll be looking right at the road-closure forms, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years. It's like the information just isn't there when I try to process it.
During those moments when your mind goes blank, do you feel as if your mind is something separate from you, or as if you are observing your own inability to think from a distance?

No, it doesn't feel like that. I'm not... watching myself from the outside or feeling disconnected from my body or anything. It's just me, standing there, realizing my head is completely empty. I'm fully there, I just don't have any thoughts going on.
